title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is written upside down. It is a scratch sheet, between pages on truncated module categories M_N (previous page) and M/Neg_∞ ≃ lim M_N (next page), and it records two threads.

(1) Presentations of divided-power (PD) envelopes. Given an ideal J ⊂ A, Grothendieck writes the PD envelope as a quotient of a free divided-power polynomial algebra A{(X_i)_{i∈I},(Y_j)_{j∈J}}. The relations are of the type ΣX_i − π, ΣY_j − ω_j, together with the corresponding differentials ΣdX_i, ΣdY_j. These look like a 'barycentric' or Čech-type presentation, with an affine-simplex constraint ΣX_i = π and its differential. That reading fits the small simplex sketched on the page.

Alternatively he presents it as Γ*_{(A,J)}(A^I ⊗_A J) modulo the relation identifying Σ X_i⊗π with π, i.e. the quotient by δJ where δπ = Σ X_i⊗π − π. He also writes a principal-ideal version A{(X_i)}/(Σ πX_i − π, πΣdX_i).

The aim seems to be to describe the PD envelope Γ*_{(A,J)}(…)/δJ, and the canonical map Γ*_A J → J (degree ≥1 part to the ideal), in a form usable for the divided-power de Rham complex.

(2) Divided powers in (co)homology. The claim 'H_*(X,□)^* : p.d.' says the cohomology ring carries a PD structure. The maps:
- H^{2i}(X,M) → H^{2iα}(X,Γ^α M): the divided-power operation x ↦ x^{[α]}, defined for even-degree classes with coefficients in a module M.
- H^{2i}(X,J) → H^{2iα}(X,Γ^α J) → H^{2iα}(X,J): uses the PD structure Γ^α J → J of the ideal to land back in J-coefficients.
- Γ^i M → Sym^i M, with x^{(i)} ↦ x^i and x^i = i! x^{(i)}: the usual comparison between divided and symmetric powers.

The intended use is presumably to show that cohomology (de Rham or crystalline-type) with coefficients in a PD ideal inherits divided powers in even degrees.
errors: No mathematical errors are visible. The relations in the presentations are only sketched: which relations generate the kernel, and whether ΣdX_i is meant in a de Rham complex, is not specified.
The map H^{2i}(X,M) → H^{2iα}(X,Γ^α M) needs an E∞ / Steenrod-type cochain structure (or a simplicial commutative setting) to be well defined. The page does not justify this.

ideas.what: Presentation of the PD envelope of an ideal as a quotient of a free divided-power polynomial algebra with simplex-type relations (ΣX_i = π, ΣdX_i = 0)
ideas.modern_name: divided power envelope D_A(J); PD polynomial algebras

ideas.what: Divided-power operations on even-degree cohomology, H^{2i}(X,M) → H^{2iα}(X,Γ^α M), composed with Γ^α J → J
ideas.modern_name: divided power operations / PD structure on even (co)homology
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Cartan (1954-55 seminar, divided powers in homology of commutative DG algebras / Eilenberg–MacLane spaces); Steenrod-type constructions

ideas.what: Comparison Γ^i M → Sym^i M with x^i = i! x^{(i)}
ideas.modern_name: canonical map from divided powers to symmetric powers

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard working notes on PD envelopes and divided-power operations in cohomology, all classical (Cartan, Roby, Berthelot). The simplex-type presentation is only sketched and is not developed into anything new.
transcription_corrections: The page is written upside down.
'Sy_m × M' is likely Sym^i M or Γ^α M (cf. 'Γ^i M → Sym^i M').
'A ⟶(2i) M' and 'Γ^α M  2α' are degree annotations (a class of degree 2i; Γ^α of it lies in degree 2iα).
